ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are three squares in the figure. The lower square is labeled 144, and its upper side is a horizontal line; the small square on the right is labeled 25, and its left side is a vertical line; the tilted square in the upper left is labeled 169, and one of its sides connects the left endpoint and the upper endpoint of the internal triangle. The internal triangle is enclosed by the upper side of the 144 square, the left side of the 25 square, and one slanted side of the 169 square, and a right angle is marked in the figure at the intersection of the horizontal side and the vertical side. Reasoning: The problem gives the areas of the three squares, so their side lengths are respectively sqrt(144)=12, sqrt(25)=5, and sqrt(169)=13. The two mutually perpendicular sides of the internal triangle are exactly the sides of lengths 12 and 5, so the area of the triangle is (1/2)×12×5=30.

raw_record.question_text: Given the areas of the three squares in the figure, what is the area of the interior triangle?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the interior triangle is bounded by the top side of the square labeled 144, the left side of the square labeled 25, and the adjacent side of the tilted square labeled 169. The right-angle marker shows the 144-square side and 25-square side are perpendicular. From the text, the numbers are areas of squares, so their side lengths are sqrt(144)=12, sqrt(25)=5, and sqrt(169)=13. Use the two perpendicular sides of the interior triangle as base and height: area = (1/2)(12)(5)=30.
